findings.issue: releaseProvision clears provision_claimed_at with only `provider_order_id IS NULL` as the guard, so it does not check that the lease still belongs to the caller. Suppose holder A outlives its lease, for example through a GC pause or a response that trickles in so the socket read timeout never fires. Waiter B takes over. A then fails and releases B's live lease, so waiter C can take over at once. B and C both call createOrder. The conditional publish still stores exactly one id, so this only adds orphan orders, never a second payable one. Two related points: the release runs on any RuntimeException, timeouts included, which is broader than the CTO's 'definitive failure' wording but has the same orphan-only worst case; and if releaseProvision itself throws (DB down), it masks the original Razorpay exception.
findings.fix: Scope the release to the caller's own claim. Carry the claimed timestamp through, or `RETURNING provision_claimed_at` from insertClaimed/reclaimProvision, and add `AND provision_claimed_at = :claimedAt`. Wrap the release in try/catch and use e.addSuppressed so the original cause is kept. Optionally reword the comment to say that a timeout is treated as a failure and that an orphan is the accepted worst case.

findings.issue: V8 was edited after review at d17de779, so its checksum changed. validate-on-migrate is true, so any database that already applied the earlier V8 (a shared dev or staging DB, not Testcontainers) will refuse to start. That is safe, but a deploy surprise. The CTO ruling (d) covers the edit itself.
findings.fix: Before merge, confirm that no persistent environment ran the d17de779 V8. If one did, run `flyway repair` there under Owner control, or reset that DB.

summary: I approve this delta with minors only. Releasing the lease cannot produce two published orders or two payable orders handed out. Take a timeout where Razorpay did create order A: we never received A's id, so it is never published and never returned to anyone. The customer cannot pay an order id they were never given, so A is an orphan, the same worst case the CTO already accepted for lease takeover. A retry takes the NULL lease through reclaimProvision, creates order B, and the conditional publish (`provider_order_id IS NULL`) still stores at most one id. Every caller then answers with the stored row. The one weakness is that the release is not scoped to the caller's own lease, which can add extra orphan createOrder calls but not a second payable order (minor). The publish guard closes the switchProvider race. A row switched to STRIPE while the holder waits on Razorpay now fails the publish on `mode = 'RAZORPAY'`, takes the existing WARN path and returns the stored STRIPE row. A switch back to RAZORPAY sets its own order id first, so the late publish fails on `provider_order_id IS NULL`. The test also covers a status change to FAILED. The remaining case, switchProvider running after a successful publish, is the existing backlog (2) issue: a Razorpay order cannot be cancelled. Startup validation is fail-fast. PaymentProperties has two constructors and no @ConstructorBinding, so it binds through setters, and binding (ConfigurationPropertiesBindingPostProcessor, PriorityOrdered) runs before @PostConstruct. A bad value therefore throws IllegalStateException during bean creation and aborts the context. The defaults pass (18s > 3s+10s), and the integration test now sets 500ms+500ms timeouts so its 2s lease stays valid. V8's `SET LOCAL lock_timeout = '5s'` works under Flyway. Flyway runs each Postgres migration in its own transaction by default, this config does not override that, and V8 has no non-transactional statements. The setting is scoped to the migration transaction and does not leak into the pooled session. Its only side effect is the checksum change (minor). All five round-1 minors are resolved: (1) the publish guard on mode, status and method was added; (2) the lease, watch interval and alert durations are validated at startup; (3) V8 has a lock_timeout and the runbook says 'brief exclusive lock'; (4) the misleading CONCURRENTLY pre-create advice was removed; (5) the LEDGER MISMATCH runbook row names the roughly 24h Razorpay retry window. The delta adds no endpoints, auth changes, dependencies, new SQL concatenation of input (all parameters are bound), or secrets or PII in logs.
